::: {.callout-note}
**Audience:** collaborators designing one end-of-Week-1 figure.  
**Metaphor:** a **message board** of small **notes** — a visual glossary.  
**Optional layer:** sticky “lab links” on notes where a Bern group clearly lives on that idea.
:::

## One idea

Students leave Week 1 with four words that felt natural in the Bajau / Tibetan stories.

The figure is **not** a research org chart and **not** a cascade diagram.

It is a **glossary on a board**:

> Here is what we meant — and how slippery it is.  
> If you want to see people who work on this nearby, peek at the lab stickers.

---

## Layout (for the artist)

### Board

- Soft cork / pinboard / wall background (simple; not cluttered).
- Title strip, e.g. **“Words we used casually”** or **“A pocket glossary for today”**.

### Notes (required)

Four larger note cards — one per concept. Each card has the same structure:

| Zone on the note | Content |
|---|---|
| **Header** | Concept name (*population* / *gene* / *generation* / *selection*) |
| **In class today** | 1 short line: how the word showed up (Bajau / Tibetans / models) |
| **But wait…** | 1–2 lines: the ambiguity / hard question |
| **For a model we’d need…** | 1 line: what must be specified |

Keep typography calm. Same card template repeated four times = readable glossary.

### Lab stickers (optional, secondary)

Smaller tags pinned to a note (or hanging from it), e.g. `Bank Lab`, `Peichel`, …  

Rules:

- Stickers are **examples**, not a full faculty list.
- A name can appear on more than one note if honest.
- Empty sticker slots OK (“add later”).
- Visual weight: **notes first**, stickers second (smaller type, muted colour).

---

## Copy for the four notes

Edit freely; this is starter text for the board.

### Note 1 — Population

- **In class today:** “the Bajau,” “Tibetans,” later: lakes, cages, demes in models.
- **But wait…** A lake population is easy to draw a boundary around. Humans (and many species) are more continuous in space — who is in / out?
- **For a model we’d need…** A definition of the set of individuals (and how they connect by migration).
- **Lab stickers (optional):** Seehausen · Allan · Peischl

### Note 2 — Gene

- **In class today:** PDE10A, BDKRB2, FAM178B, EPAS1 — “genes” linked to adaptation.
- **But wait…** Coding sequence? Regulatory region? Whole haplotype? A name as proxy for a causal change?
- **For a model we’d need…** A clear physical object (what mutates, what is tracked).
- **Lab stickers (optional):** Peichel · Pertz · Bank

### Note 3 — Generation

- **In class today:** adaptations unfold “over generations”; discrete update steps in models.
- **But wait…** Discrete vs continuous time? Overlapping generations? How long is a human generation?
- **For a model we’d need…** A clock (and whether generations overlap).
- **Lab stickers (optional):** Ringler · *(course Weeks 2–7)*

### Note 4 — Selection

- **In class today:** alleles “favoured,” haplotypes “swept,” diving / highland adaptation.
- **But wait…** Can we give a gene *an* effect \(s\)? It depends on **environment** — and on **which genome / individual**.
- **For a model we’d need…** Fitness measured relative to a specified background and setting.
- **Lab stickers (optional):** **Bank** (epistasis / genome-dependent effects) · Ringler · Peichel · Seehausen

**Optional fifth mini-note (only if space):**  
*Epistasis* — when the effect of a mutation depends on the rest of the genome. Natural bridge from the *selection* note → Bank Lab sticker.

## Lab sticker key (for collaborators; not all text must appear on the art)

| Sticker | Tiny gloss (≤6 words if on figure) |
|---|---|
| Bank | epistasis · fitness interactions |
| Peichel | genetic basis of adaptation |
| Seehausen | populations → species / radiations |
| Ringler | individuals · behaviour · fitness |
| Allan | communities · coexistence |
| Pertz | cell signalling dynamics |
| Peischl | spatial populations · rescue |

---

## Do / don’t

**Do**

- Glossary first: four notes readable in 30 seconds
- Same card structure for every concept
- Lab links as optional stickers

**Don’t**

- Hub-and-spoke org maps or long cascades as the main design
- Equal-weight wall of logos
- Implying Week 1 teaches each lab’s research

> “We used these words like everyone knows them. Here they are as a little glossary — and a few sticky notes for labs next door that live on the same ideas.”
